subject: Your 7-day Money Reset starts now
preview: One small box a day. Day 1 arrives tomorrow.
body:
Welcome.

This is the Money Reset: seven boxes, one a day, about 10 minutes each. In a week your money runs on rules instead of willpower.

The whole checklist is here if you like to see it all at once: https://youngstunners88.github.io/quiet-money/money-reset/

Tomorrow's box: find the leaks. Hit reply if you get stuck.

subject: Day 1: find the leaks
body:
Open last month's bank and card statements. Highlight every subscription and recurring charge. Cancel at least one you forgot about.

Why it matters: a $15 a month subscription costs $1,800 over 10 years. Invested instead at an assumed 8% a year, that same $15 a month would be about $2,744. Small leaks are not small.

Today's box: one cancellation. That is the whole job.

subject: Day 2: pay yourself first
preview: Saving what's left is why nothing is left.
body:
Open a separate savings account and set an automatic transfer for payday. Even $25.

Why it matters: $25 a month for 30 years at an assumed 8% a year grows to about $37,259, and you only put in $9,000. The amount matters less than the habit and the time.

Today's box: the automatic transfer, set once.

subject: Day 3: split every paycheck
body:
Write your take-home pay. Then split it: 50% needs, 30% wants, 20% future.

On $4,000 a month that is $2,000 for needs, $1,200 for wants and $800 for your future. If your needs are over 50%, circle the biggest one. That is next month's project, not today's.

Today's box: the three numbers on one piece of paper.

subject: Day 4: attack the expensive debt first
body:
List every debt with its interest rate. Put every extra dollar on the highest rate (avalanche) or the smallest balance (snowball). Pick one and stick to it.

Why it matters: $6,000 at 24% paid at a typical minimum takes about 21 years and costs $10,887 in interest. The minimum is not a plan.

Today's box: the list, and one choice of method.

subject: Day 5: build the $1,000 buffer
preview: A surprise bill should not become a debt.
body:
Sell one thing you do not use, do a no-spend weekend, and park the cash in savings labeled emergencies only.

Why it matters: a $600 surprise put on a 24% card costs about $144 a year in interest while you carry it. A buffer turns a crisis into an inconvenience.

Today's box: the first $100 of the $1,000. Start there.

subject: Day 6: stop fee bleeding
preview: Banks waive fees when you ask.
body:
Turn on low-balance and large-purchase alerts in your banking app. Then look at the last 90 days of fees and ask your bank: "Can you waive this as a courtesy?"

Why it matters: one $35 fee a quarter is $140 a year. Alerts stop most of them before they happen.

Today's box: alerts on, and one phone call.

subject: Day 7: lock in your raises
preview: Decide now, while it is easy.
body:
Write this rule down: when income goes up, half the raise goes to savings before I see it. Put your money rules on one index card and keep it in your wallet.

Why it matters: on a $3,000 a year raise, half is $125 a month. Invested at an assumed 8% a year for 20 years it grows to about $73,628, and you never felt it leave.

You finished the Money Reset. Reply and tell me which box changed the most for you.
